nodes.name: Sequential Anodization Dehydration Phosphorization
nodes.procedure: CP NW arrays were synthesized on CF via sequential anodization, dehydration, and phosphorization. On the anodized CF, uniform Cu(OH)2 NWs are observed with a diameter around 100 nm. After dehydration, the sky-blue Cu(OH)2 transforms into black CuO. The NWs are slightly curved after further phosphorization. The crystallized CP NW possesses a smooth surface with a diameter of around 200 nm.

nodes.name: In Situ Growth of CLDH
nodes.procedure: 20 mL of cobalt (II) nitrate methanol solution (0.05 M) was mixed with 5 mL of deionized (DI) water and 20 mL of 2-methylimidazole methanol solution (0.2 M), and 4 pieces of CuO/CF were immersed into the mixed solution. The reaction was kept at room temperature for 4 h. The final sample was washed with excessive DI water and dried in a vacuum oven.

nodes.name: Phosphorization of CLDH/CuO/CF
nodes.procedure: 500 mg of sodium hypophosphite powder was supplied in the upstream furnace and 4 pieces of CLDH/CuO/CF were placed in the downstream one (See the illustration in Figure S1, Supporting Information). The sodium hypophosphite was heated at 5°C min⁻¹ and kept at 300°C for 1 h. Meanwhile, the CLDH/CuO/CF was heated at 2°C min⁻¹ and kept at 150°C for 1 h. The furnaces were cooled down to room temperature naturally.

nodes.name: Phosphatization of Powders
nodes.procedure: To lay the foundation for the construction of CF-supported semiconductor junction, the CLDH and CuO powders were first phosphatized at 150°C (Figure S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks assigned to (003) plane of CLDH (PDF#53-0916) and (112), (202), (211), (113), and (300) planes of Cu₃P (PDF#02-1263).
nodes.evidence_snippet: After phosphorization of CLDH/CuO/CF, the diffraction peaks assigned to (003) plane of CLDH (PDF#53-0916) and (112), (202), (211), (113), and (300) planes of Cu₃P (PDF#02-1263) are clearly observed, as shown in Figure 2a.

nodes.characterization_summary: Non-collapsing morphology of laminalike CLDH NSs and vein-like CP NWs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images in Figure 2b,c presents the non-collapsing morphology of laminalike CLDH NSs and vein-like CP NWs.

nodes.characterization_summary: CLDH NS integrated with CP NW with visible boundary and macropores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images in Figure 2d,e displays the CLDH NS is integrated with the CP NW with visible boundary and macropores.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes with spacing of 0.211 nm associated with (200) facet of CoO; 0.202 nm and 0.176 nm correspond to (300) and (220) planes of Cu₃P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM in Figure 2f exhibits several lattice fringes with a spacing of 0.211 nm is associated with the (200) facet of CoO... Another two sets of lattice fringe with interplanar spacings of 0.202 and 0.176 nm respectively correspond to the (300) and (220) planes of Cu₃P.

nodes.characterization_summary: Wider distribution of Co and O elements than Cu and P elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2g, the energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mapping images confirm the wider distribution of Co and O elements than that of Cu and P elements.

properties.description: Multi-panel image labeled g, showing elemental mapping of nanoparticles

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu 2p: Cu^I at 932.6 eV, Cu^II at 934.6 eV and satellite at 946 eV; P 2p: Cu-P at 129.5 eV, P-O at 133.6 eV; Co 2p: Co^III at 779.9 eV, Co^II at 781.4 eV and satellite at 789 eV. Shifts in binding energies indicate charge transfer from CLDH to CP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2h, the Cu 2p spectra are deconvolved into Cu^I at 932.6 eV Cu^II at 934.6 eV and a satellite at around 946 eV. In Figure 2i, the P 2p spectra show Cu-P at around 129.5 eV and P-O at 133.6 eV... For the Co 2p spectra in Figure 2j, Co^III at 779.9 eV, Co^II at 781.4 eV and shakeup satellite at around 789 eV are distinguished... It is investigated that the Cu 2p, Co 2p, P 2p, and O 1s XPS spectra of CLDH/CP/CF shift in binding energies compared to those of CP/CF and CLDH/CF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bandgap of CLDH is 2.45 eV and CP is 1.68 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Kubelka-Munk plots (Figure S3, Supporting Information) determine the bandgap of CLDH and CP are 2.45 and 1.68 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Positive slope for CLDH (n-type) and negative slope for CP (p-type); flat band potentials -0.19 V and 1.59 V vs RHE respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Mott-Schottky plots (Figure S4, Supporting Information) show the positive slope of CLDH and negative slope of CP... the flat band potentials (E_FB), that is, Fermi levels (E_F) of CLDH and CP are determined to be -0.19 and 1.59 V versus RHE, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Good crystallinity of Cu₃P and derived CoO confirmed by SAED pattern.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The good crystallinity of Cu₃P and derived CoO is also proved by the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Figure S9, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s spectra present metal-O at 529.6 eV, metal-OH at 531.5 eV, and P-O at 530.4 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the O 1s spectra (Figure S10, Supporting Information) present metal-O at 529.6 eV, metal-OH at 531.5 eV, and P-O at 530.4 eV.
